title: DO VISION-LANGUAGE MODELS REPRESENT SPACE AND HOW? EVALUATING SPATIAL FRAME OF REFERENCE UNDER AMBIGUITIES

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting vision-language models with ambiguous spatial relationship queries across 109 different languages to determine if their implicit spatial reasoning defaults to English linguistic conventions (e.g., egocentric relative frame of reference) rather than respecting the native conventions of the target language.

Evaluating model predictions on spatial relationships across diverse regions to see if the models flexibly adopt non-Western/non-English cultural conventions for coordinate transformations (e.g., translated vs. reflected projections) or if they disproportionately favor English-centric cultural norms.
